findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the seeded vendor-roster spreadsheet) are stored without an enforced default encryption policy under customer control.
No ACL is declared and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so bucket or object ACLs and bucket policies could grant anonymous access with no preventive guardrail.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial ledger data at rest without an enforced default encryption policy.

A private ACL is set but no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block enforces blocking of public ACLs or policies, so there is no defence-in-depth against an accidental public grant on sensitive financial data.
The model artifacts bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored artifacts and any embedded training data are not encrypted under an enforced default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the bucket relies solely on its ACL to remain private with no guardrail against a future public ACL or bucket policy.
The runbooks bucket defines no default server-side encryption configuration, and operational runbooks commonly contain infrastructure detail and procedural secrets.
The bucket lacks an associated aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a future ACL or policy change could expose runbook contents publicly with no preventive control.
The log aggregation bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; nothing prevents a public ACL or bucket policy being added to a bucket that concentrates access logs from other buckets.

The audit/log-delivery bucket sets force_destroy = true with no object lock or MFA delete, so a principal with bucket-level permissions can destroy the entire audit trail, defeating the integrity of security logging.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on data bucket
findings.description: No logging block is configured, so reads and writes of the stored reports (including the seeded vendor roster) produce no S3 access log trail for detecting or investigating unauthorized access.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on data bucket
findings.description: No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive ledger export data is not recorded to the audit bucket, undermining accountability and forensic capability.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on data bucket
findings.description: No logging block is present, so access to operational runbooks is untracked and enumeration of internal procedures would leave no audit trail.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on data bucket
findings.description: The audit bucket itself has no logging block, so access to the consolidated log data is not itself recorded.

The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that itself sets no default encryption, so the object is stored unencrypted by customer-controlled keys.
Neither this nor any other bucket in the file attaches a bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so unencrypted HTTP access to bucket data is not prevented.
